text:
sana: Running into weird undefined exports when I deploy an edge function with our JS SDK. Local Node (CJS) works but Vercel edge fails.

tomas: Likely an ESM/CJS mismatch. Vercel edge prefers ESM and may load the package's "import" entry. Are you using require()?

sana: Yep `const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')`. Any short workaround?

rachel_docs: Quick options:
- switch file to ESM and `import { createClient }`
- use dynamic import in your handler: `const { createClient } = await import('@redwood/inference')`
- temporary wrapper that re-exports a shape your runtime expects

tomas: For TypeScript, mention `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports`. If consumers mix CJS require and ESM package exports, typings can be wrong.

sana: Dynamic import fixed runtime but lost some TS autocompletion. Will try enabling `esModuleInterop` in the project.

rachel_docs: I'll add a short compatibility note to quickstart: ESM examples + a small CJS edge workaround snippet and a line about types flags and bundler quirks. I'll link internal ticket INF-724 for publishing a CJS fallback.

ci-bot: Created docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/421 (compat: ESM/CJS guidance)

sana: Perfect, thanks — that'll save a few support tickets.
